title: Microsoft Teams: upgraded call history in the Calls app
summary: The rollout details, calling policy controls and automatic arrival are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. Two qualifications would improve the briefing: Microsoft's support page gives different call-history licensing wording, and a newly configured call-log retention policy applies only to new logs.

claims.claim: Microsoft is upgrading call history in the Teams Calls app.
claims.quote: Call history in the Teams Calls app is being upgraded to make it easier to find and act on past call activity.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The upgrade reaches Calls app users without administrator enablement.
claims.quote: What will happen: - Missed calls and associated voicemails will be consolidated into a single call history entry. [...] No admin action is required before rollout.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific upgrade.
claims.quote: Searched: "upgraded call history" Teams; Teams upgraded call history 570843 3000 six months admin policy enable disable retention licensing. Read Teams calling overview, calling policies and search excerpts; results describe other call-history features.

claims.claim: Make private calls is reached in Teams admin center via Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Make private calls.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. [...] Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit. [...] Make private calls - This setting controls all calling capabilities in Teams.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowPrivateCalling $false disables calling in the Global policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowPrivateCalling $true [...] Controls all calling capabilities in Teams. Turning this off will turn off all calling functionality in Teams. [...] Type: Boolean

claims.claim: Make private calls is an existing all-or-nothing control for Teams calling rather than a switch specific to upgraded history.
claims.quote: Make private calls - This setting controls all calling capabilities in Teams. Turn this setting off to turn off all calling functionality in Teams.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users assigned a policy with Make private calls off cannot see the Calls app.
claims.quote: If the Make private calls setting is turned off in the calling policy, users with that policy can't see the Calls app in their Teams client

claims.claim: Voicemail for inbound calls is reached in Teams admin center via Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Voicemail for inbound calls.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Calling Policies [...] Choose the policy you would like to update [...] For Voicemail for inbound calls, select one of the following options

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowVoicemail AlwaysDisabled prevents routing inbound calls to voicemail for the Global policy.
claims.quote: this script turns off the ability for users to route inbound calls to voicemail for the Global (default) Teams Calling Policy instance: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowVoicemail AlwaysDisabled

claims.claim: Voicemail for inbound calls controls whether calls can route to voicemail.
claims.quote: You can control whether routing of calls to Cloud Voicemail is allowed for Teams users by using the Teams admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.claim: Neither calling policy setting is documented as changing the upgraded history's presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Calls app upgraded call history Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy switch call history 3000 November 2026. Read calling policies, Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy and Cloud Voicemail; these document calling availability and voicemail routing, not the upgrade's presentation.

claims.where: controls[2]; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No dedicated tenant or user switch for the upgraded call history is documented on either the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Calls app upgraded call history Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy switch call history 3000 November 2026; Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy ShowTeamsCallsInCallLog. Read calling policies, cmdlet reference and release-note excerpts; no switch for this upgrade was documented.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The upgrade is an included native Teams calling capability under the Microsoft Teams Enterprise license.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Teams Enterprise license includes native calling features. [...] Support: Your call history is available if you have an Enterprise Voice or Business Voice license as part of your Microsoft 365 subscription.
claims.fix: Keep the documented native-calling entitlement, but add: 'Microsoft's call-history support page separately says call history is available with an Enterprise Voice or Business Voice license as part of a Microsoft 365 subscription; the pages use different licensing wording.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/teams/calls-devices/view-your-call-history-in-microsoft-teams.

claims.claim: The Calls app allows users to place calls to other Teams users.
claims.quote: The Calls app in Teams allows users to originate calls to other Teams users, view call history, and access voicemail that is automatically set up for all Teams users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams call logs are retained indefinitely by default.
claims.quote: By default, Teams call logs are retained indefinitely.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: A retention policy for Teams call logs is the documented mechanism for deleting those logs.
claims.quote: Use a retention policy for call logs if you need to delete this data for compliance reasons. [...] Configuration page: The policy applies only to new call logs that are created after the policy is configured and active.
claims.fix: Add this qualification to the retention-policy statement: 'The policy applies only to new call logs created after it is configured and active.' The qualification is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies.

claims.claim: Teams call-log retention policies can be created and modified only using PowerShell.
claims.quote: This separate retention policy for call logs can be created and modified only by using PowerShell.

claims.claim: Teams call-log retention policies are visible but read-only in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: After you create the retention policy for Teams call logs, it's displayed in Data Lifecycle Management > Policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, where it's visible but read-only.
